title: Countable structure spaces, Part II: Borel reducibility of isomorphism relations and Borel completeness
summary: Compares isomorphism relations of classes of countable structures by Borel reducibility; defines Borel completeness (also for languages with function symbols); proves by explicit continuous codings that graphs, linear orders and trees are Borel complete (Friedman–Stanley); embeds every Borel S∞-space into the logic action of the language with one n-ary symbol per n (Becker–Kechris for S∞, through the Polish realization of NoncompactQuantumSymmetry); proves the characterisations of Borel completeness; and shows that a Borel complete isomorphism relation is not Borel, lies above E₀, has continuum many classes and unbounded Scott height, with the Friedman–Stanley obstruction lemma.

layers.title: Isomorphism relations of classes and two reducibilities

targets.name: classIso
targets.statement: For K : Set (StructureSpace L), classIso K : Setoid K is Setoid.comap of structureIsoSetoid L along the inclusion K → StructureSpace L; K carries the subtype σ-algebra.
hypotheses: L is a relational first-order language ([L.IsRelational]) (no countability needed for the definition)

locator.where: Definition 1.4, line 83; camerlo-gao-boolean lines 106–110 for classes

api.name: classIso_iff
api.statement: For x y : K, classIso K x y holds iff the decoded structures of x and y are isomorphic, iff x and y lie in one orbit of the logic action (structureIsoSetoid_eq_orbitRel).

api.name: borelReducible_classIso_univ
api.statement: classIso Set.univ and structureIsoSetoid L are Borel reducible to each other, the inclusion of univ being a measurable equivalence.

api.name: quotient_injection
api.statement: A Borel reduction of classIso K' to classIso K induces an injection of quotients (BorelEquivalenceRelations §5.1); it need not be injective on codes.

tests.name: two_orbit_class
tests.statement: In the language of one unary predicate, the class {P = ∅, P = ℕ} is invariant Borel and classIso of it is equality with exactly two classes; the class 'P finite' has one class per finite size.

tests.name: empty_class
tests.statement: classIso ∅ reduces to every classIso K by the empty map, and classIso K reduces to classIso ∅ iff K = ∅.

tests.name: noninjective_reduction
tests.statement: For K' the codes with P infinite and coinfinite (one orbit, uncountably many codes) and any nonempty K, the constant map reduces classIso K' to classIso K without being injective on codes.

tests.name: noninvariant_subclass
tests.statement: For A the single code P = {0} inside the class |P| = 1, the inclusion reduces classIso A to classIso K; both have one class.

targets.name: borelReducible_classIso_of_subset
targets.statement: If A ⊆ K then classIso A is Borel reducible to classIso K; hence if classIso K' is Borel reducible to classIso K and A ⊆ K', then classIso A is Borel reducible to classIso K.
hypotheses: L is a relational first-order language ([L.IsRelational])
A, K, K' arbitrary sets of codes (no Borelness needed)

tests.name: restriction_to_orbit
tests.statement: Restricting the reduction of 2.5 to the orbit of one code of StructureSpace L' gives a reduction of a one-class relation.

targets.name: borelReducible_classIso_of_measurable
targets.statement: If f : StructureSpace L' → StructureSpace L is measurable, maps K' into K, and for all x y ∈ K' the codes x, y are isomorphic iff f x, f y are, then classIso K' is Borel reducible to classIso K.
hypotheses: L is a relational first-order language ([L.IsRelational]) with countably many relation symbols ([Countable (Σ l, L.Relations l)])

targets.name: SetReducible
targets.statement: SetReducible A B for A : Set X, B : Set Y on measurable spaces: ∃ f : X → Y measurable with ∀ x, x ∈ A ↔ f x ∈ B.

api.name: SetReducible.refl/trans
api.statement: SetReducible is reflexive and transitive.

api.name: setReducible_compl_iff
api.statement: SetReducible A B ↔ SetReducible Aᶜ Bᶜ.

api.name: SetReducible.measurableSet
api.statement: SetReducible A B and MeasurableSet B give MeasurableSet A.

api.name: SetReducible.analyticSet
api.statement: For X, Y Polish with Borel σ-algebras, SetReducible A B and AnalyticSet B give AnalyticSet A (refine the topology by Measurable.exists_continuous, then AnalyticSet.preimage).

tests.name: singleton_to_diagonal
tests.statement: A = {0} ⊆ ℕ, B the diagonal of Cantor space squared: the map 0 ↦ (0,0), n+1 ↦ (0,1) has preimage {0}.

tests.name: empty_and_univ_targets
tests.statement: A is set reducible to ∅ iff A = ∅ and to univ iff A = univ.

tests.name: nonborel_not_reducible
tests.statement: The complement of the base's wellOrderClass is analytic and not Borel, so it is not set reducible to the (Borel) diagonal.

tests.name: equality_pullback
tests.statement: For injective measurable f, the graph of equality on X is the preimage of the diagonal of Y under Prod.map f f.

targets.name: setReducible_graph_of_borelReducible
targets.statement: If BorelReducible E F for setoids E on X and F on Y, then {p | E p.1 p.2} is SetReducible to {p | F p.1 p.2}, by Prod.map f f.

targets.name: setReducible_eZero_diagonal
targets.statement: The graph of eZero is SetReducible to the diagonal of (ℕ → Bool) × (ℕ → Bool), whereas eZero is not BorelReducible to (⊥ : Setoid (ℕ → Bool)); so set reducibility of graphs does not imply Borel reducibility.

targets.name: StructureSpaceOn.relabel
targets.statement: For any language L and e : α ≃ β, the map StructureSpaceOn L α → StructureSpaceOn L β sending c to the code with value c ⟨R, e.symm ∘ w⟩ at ⟨R, w⟩; a homeomorphism and measurable equivalence.

locator.where: lines 159–164 (the logic action as relabelling of structures on ℕ)

api.name: relabel_trans/relabel_refl
api.statement: Relabelling along e.trans e' is the composite and along Equiv.refl is the identity; inverse along e.symm.

api.name: relabel_perm
api.statement: For α = β = ℕ, relabelling along σ is the logic action σ • ·.

api.name: relabel_eq_encodeVia
api.statement: For relational L, the relabelled code is encodeVia e of the decoded structure; c and its relabelling decode to isomorphic structures.

api.name: relabel_iso_iff
api.statement: Two codes on α are isomorphic iff their relabellings are; invariant Borel classes map to invariant Borel classes.

tests.name: transposition
tests.statement: Relabelling P = {0} along the transposition (0 1) gives P = {1}, equal to the logic action.

tests.name: fin_zero
tests.statement: On Fin 0 the coding space of a language without nullary symbols is one point and relabelling is the identity; with one nullary symbol, two fixed points.

tests.name: three_cycle_twice
tests.statement: Relabelling P = {0} twice along the 3-cycle 0→1→2→0 gives P = {2} ≠ {0}, while relabelling along e then e.symm is the identity.

targets.name: BorelComplete
targets.statement: BorelComplete K for K : Set (StructureSpace L): for every L' : Language.{0,0} with [L'.IsRelational] [Countable (Σ l, L'.Relations l)] and every K' : Set (StructureSpace L') with MeasurableSet K' and IsomorphismInvariant K', BorelReducible (classIso K') (classIso K).
hypotheses: L is a relational first-order language ([L.IsRelational]) with countably many relation symbols ([Countable (Σ l, L.Relations l)])

api.name: BorelComplete.of_borelReducible
api.statement: BorelComplete K and BorelReducible (classIso K) (classIso K₂) give BorelComplete K₂; in particular K ⊆ K₂.

api.name: borelComplete_congr
api.statement: Borel completeness depends only on classIso K up to Borel bireducibility.

api.name: BorelComplete.borelReducible_univ
api.statement: If BorelComplete K then every invariant Borel class of a countable relational language in any universes reduces to K (target 1.3).

api.name: borelComplete_map_lequiv_iff
api.statement: For e : L ≃ᴸ L₂, K is Borel complete iff its image under the code-space homeomorphism of e is.

tests.name: empty_not_complete
tests.statement: BorelComplete ∅ fails: K' = univ for one unary symbol is nonempty.

tests.name: countably_many_types
tests.statement: The class of codes of one unary predicate is not Borel complete: the closed class of codes of countably many unary predicates each ∅ or ℕ has types in bijection with ℕ → Bool and cannot inject into a countable quotient.

tests.name: union_not_intersection
tests.statement: If K is Borel complete so is K ∪ K₂; graphClass ∩ (orbit of the empty graph) is one orbit and not Borel complete.

tests.name: renaming
tests.statement: Renaming adj in Language.graph gives an equivalent language and the image of graphClass is Borel complete.

targets.name: BorelComplete.borelReducible_univ
targets.statement: If BorelComplete K, then for every L' : Language.{u', v'} with [L'.IsRelational] [Countable (Σ l, L'.Relations l)] and every invariant Borel K' ⊆ StructureSpace L', classIso K' is Borel reducible to classIso K.
hypotheses: L is a relational first-order language ([L.IsRelational]) with countably many relation symbols ([Countable (Σ l, L.Relations l)])
L' countable relational in arbitrary universes

locator.where: lines 87–93 and 101–105 (Mod(L) for an arbitrary countable language)

targets.name: FunCode
targets.statement: For L with countably many function and relation symbols, the functional coding space: pairs (F, c) of a table F : (Σ f : (Σ l, L.Functions l), Fin f.1 → ℕ) → ℕ and a relation code c : StructureSpace L, with the product topology; decoding to L.Structure ℕ; the action (σ • F)⟨f, v⟩ = σ (F ⟨f, σ⁻¹ ∘ v⟩) and the logic action on c.

locator.where: lines 60–64 (groups, abelian groups and torsion-free abelian groups as Borel subsets of the space of structures)

api.name: polishSpace_funCode
api.statement: The functional coding space is Polish and the action is continuous.

api.name: orbitRel_funCode_iff
api.statement: Two points lie in one orbit iff their decoded L-structures are isomorphic.

api.name: measurableSet_models
api.statement: The models on ℕ of a set of first-order L-sentences form an invariant Borel set (target 1.6).

api.name: funCode_relational
api.statement: For relational L the table is the empty map and the space is StructureSpace L.

tests.name: constant_symbol
tests.statement: For one constant symbol k, a table is one number F k; the table F k = 3 decodes to the structure interpreting k as 3.

tests.name: no_symbols
tests.statement: For the empty language the functional coding space is a single point.

tests.name: orbit_of_constant
tests.statement: Two tables F k = 3 and F k = 5 are in one orbit (transposition (3 5)), while a table and a non-isomorphic relation code are not.

targets.name: graphCodeFun_homeomorph
targets.statement: The graph-code map from the functional coding space to StructureSpace (graphLanguage L), sending a point to the code of graphExpansion of its decoded structure, is continuous, injective and equivariant; its range is the Gδ set of codes whose graph relations are graphs of total functions, which is not closed when L has at least one function symbol and is the whole coding space when L is relational; it is a homeomorphism onto its range, agreeing there with reconstructStructure; and two points decode to isomorphic structures iff their graph codes are isomorphic.
hypotheses: L with countably many function and relation symbols

tests.name: constant_graph
tests.statement: For one constant symbol and F k = 3, the unary graph relation is {3}.

tests.name: not_in_range
tests.statement: A graph code whose unary-function relation holds at (0,1) and (0,2), or at no (0,y), is not in the range; codes with value n at 0 converge as n → ∞ to a code with no value at 0, so the range is not closed.

tests.name: relational_case
tests.statement: For relational L the map is the base coding composed with the symbol relabelling R ↦ base R, and its range is the whole coding space, which is closed.

targets.name: measurableSet_funCode_models
targets.statement: For a set T of first-order L-sentences, the set of points of the functional coding space whose decoded structure is a model of T is measurable and invariant.
hypotheses: L with countably many function and relation symbols

tests.name: simple_graphs
tests.statement: For Language.graph and Theory.simpleGraph the set is graphClass.

tests.name: fields_char_two
tests.statement: For Language.ring and Theory.fieldOfChar 2 the set contains a code of 𝔽₂(t) and no code of ℚ.

targets.name: BorelComplete.borelReducible_funCode
targets.statement: If K₀ ⊆ StructureSpace L₀ is Borel complete, then for every L' with countably many function and relation symbols and every invariant Borel class K' of the functional coding space of L', the isomorphism relation of K' is Borel reducible to classIso K₀; an invariant Borel class K of a functional coding space is called Borel complete when its graph-code image is.

layers.title: Every countable structure codes into a graph

targets.name: incidenceGraph
targets.statement: For countable relational L' and an injection ι of its relation symbols into ℕ, the coloured graph H_c on points p_a (a ∈ ℕ), tuple vertices t_q, position vertices s_{q,j} (j < arity) and truth vertices u_q (q : RelQueryOn L' ℕ), coloured κ(p) = 0, κ(u) = 1, κ(s_{q,j}) = 2+2j, κ(t_{⟨R,v⟩}) = 3+2ι(R), with edges t_q—s_{q,j}, s_{q,j}—p_{v j}, and t_q—u_q iff c q = true.
hypotheses: L' relational with countably many relation symbols

locator.where: Theorem VI.27, lines 4582–4594 (coding a structure by gadgets attached to tuples; different gadgets)

api.name: incidenceGraph_bipartite
api.statement: H_c is bipartite (points and tuple vertices against positions and truth vertices), hence triangle-free.

api.name: incidenceGraph_adj_continuous
api.statement: Only tuple–truth edges depend on c, each on one coordinate c q.

api.name: incidenceGraph_iso_iff
api.statement: c ≅ d iff some colour-preserving bijection of base vertices maps H_c onto H_d (target 2.2).

tests.name: one_binary_edge
tests.statement: For R = {(0,1)}: t_{⟨R,![0,1]⟩} has three neighbours, t_{⟨R,![1,0]⟩} two.

tests.name: empty_language
tests.statement: For L' with no relation symbols, H_c has only points and no edges.

tests.name: nullary_symbol
tests.statement: A nullary symbol gives a tuple vertex without position neighbours, joined to its truth vertex iff the code says true.

tests.name: colours_needed
tests.statement: With two unary symbols, the codes P₁ = {0} and P₂ = {0} are not isomorphic but have isomorphic uncoloured incidence graphs.

targets.name: incidenceGraph_iso_iff
targets.statement: For codes c, d ∈ StructureSpace L': c and d are isomorphic iff there is a colour-preserving graph isomorphism H_c ≅ H_d.

targets.name: cliqueTag
targets.statement: For a triangle-free simple graph H on V with κ : V → ℕ, the tagged graph on V ⊕ Σ x, Fin (κ x + 3): H, a clique on the tag vertices of each x, and an edge from x to its tag vertex 0. Two triangle-free coloured graphs have isomorphic tagged graphs iff they are colour-isomorphic.

locator.where: Theorem VI.27, lines 4623–4654 (flags distinguishing coded vertices)

api.name: mem_triangle_iff_tag
api.statement: A vertex lies in a triangle iff it is a tag vertex.

api.name: cliqueTag_adj_base
api.statement: Edges between non-tag vertices are those of H.

api.name: cliqueTag_colour
api.statement: For non-tag x, κ x + 2 is the number of triangle vertices adjacent to the unique triangle-vertex neighbour of x.

tests.name: single_edge
tests.statement: One edge {x,y} with κ = (0,1): 9 vertices and 12 edges.

tests.name: empty
tests.statement: V = ∅ gives the empty graph.

tests.name: triangle_breaks
tests.statement: In the tagged graph of a triangle the original vertices lie in triangles, so the recognition rule fails without triangle-freeness.

tests.name: colour_detected
tests.statement: The tagged one-vertex graphs with κ = 0 and κ = 1 have 4 and 5 vertices and are not isomorphic.

targets.name: graphClass
targets.statement: graphClass : Set (StructureSpace Language.graph) is the set of codes whose decoded adj is irreflexive and symmetric (models of Theory.simpleGraph).

api.name: isClosed_graphClass
api.statement: graphClass is closed and invariant.

api.name: range_graphCode
api.statement: graphClass = range graphCode, and graphCode is a measurable equivalence SimpleGraph ℕ ≃ graphClass.

api.name: mem_graphClass_iff
api.statement: c ∈ graphClass iff ∀ i, ¬ adj(i,i) and ∀ i j, adj(i,j) → adj(j,i).

tests.name: empty_graph
tests.statement: The code of the empty graph is in graphClass.

tests.name: loop
tests.statement: A code with adj(0,0) is not in graphClass; one with adj(0,1) and not adj(1,0) is not.

tests.name: one_edge_orbit
tests.statement: The codes of the one-edge graphs on {0,1} and {5,7} are isomorphic; the one-edge graph and the two-edge path are not.

tests.name: clopen_conditions
tests.statement: Membership depends only on the values at adj(i,i), adj(i,j), adj(j,i): an intersection of clopen sets.

targets.name: borelComplete_graphClass
targets.statement: BorelComplete graphClass, witnessed for each L' by one continuous map StructureSpace L' → StructureSpace Language.graph (relabelled tagged incidence graph) that lands in graphClass and reflects and preserves isomorphism.

locator.where: Theorem 1; statement also at camerlo-gao-boolean lines 111–112 and paolini-shelah-tfab line 125

targets.name: ratColour
targets.statement: ν : ℚ → ℕ, ν r = padicValNat 2 r.den; each fibre ν⁻¹(m) is dense in ℚ and the fibres partition ℚ.

locator.where: Lemma VI.18, lines 4258–4260 (maps onto children with dense preimages)

api.name: dense_ratColour_preimage
api.statement: For every m, ν⁻¹(m) is dense in ℚ.

api.name: ratColour_eq_iff
api.statement: ν r = m iff the reduced denominator r.den is 2^m times an odd number.

tests.name: integers
tests.statement: Every integer has colour 0.

tests.name: half_not_zero
tests.statement: ν(1/2) = 1 ≠ 0, so the colour of 1/2 differs from that of 1.

targets.name: exists_orderIso_ratColour
targets.statement: For every bijection σ of ℕ there is an order automorphism π of ℚ with ν (π r) = σ (ν r) for all r.

locator.where: Lemma VI.18, lines 4273–4275 (dense labelled orders with dense labels are isomorphic)

tests.name: identity
tests.statement: σ = id: π = id works.

tests.name: swap
tests.statement: σ = swap(0,1): π sends 1/2 (colour 1) to a rational of colour 0.

tests.name: density_needed
tests.statement: For the two-colouring negative/non-negative, the colour swap has no order automorphism: the negatives are an initial segment and the non-negatives are not.

targets.name: unravelColour
targets.statement: For c ∈ graphClass with graph G and x : List ℚ, a(x) = x.map ν and χ_c(x) ∈ ℕ an injective encoding of (|x|, atomic diagram of a(x) in G: equalities and adjacencies of entries).

locator.where: Lemma VI.18, lines 4205–4211 and 4262–4265 (labels coding atomic diagrams and lengths)

api.name: unravelColour_length
api.statement: χ_c x determines |x|.

api.name: unravelColour_eq_iff
api.statement: χ_c x = χ_d y iff |x| = |y| and a(x), a(y) have the same atomic type in the two graphs (SameAtomicType).

api.name: unravelColour_continuous
api.statement: For fixed x, χ_c x depends on finitely many coordinates of c.

tests.name: edge_pairs
tests.statement: For G the edge {0,1}: a([1/2,1]) = (1,0), adjacent and distinct; a([1,2]) = (0,0), equal.

tests.name: short_nodes
tests.statement: χ of [] and of every node of length 1 is the same for all graphs.

tests.name: identity_fails
tests.statement: The one-edge graphs on {0,1} and {0,2} are isomorphic but differ at [1,1/2], so the identity is not colour-preserving between them.

targets.name: unravel_iso_iff
targets.statement: For c, d ∈ graphClass the following are equivalent: (i) c ≅ d; (ii) some order automorphism Φ of List ℚ has χ_d ∘ Φ = χ_c; (iii) some bijection Ψ of List ℚ preserving the parent relation (both ways) has χ_d ∘ Ψ = χ_c.
hypotheses: List ℚ with Mathlib's lexicographic order

tests.name: dense_order
tests.statement: List ℚ is densely ordered with least element []: between [0] and [0,5] lies [0,4]; [] < [-1].

tests.name: parent_definable
tests.statement: The parent of [1/2, 3] is [1/2]: the unique node of length 1 below it with no node of length < 2 strictly between.

targets.name: linearOrderClass
targets.statement: linearOrderClass : Set (StructureSpace Language.order): codes whose decoded relation is a linear order (models of Language.order.linearOrderTheory).

api.name: isClosed_linearOrderClass
api.statement: linearOrderClass is closed and invariant.

api.name: mem_linearOrderClass_orderStructure
api.statement: The code of a linear order on ℕ with orderStructure is in linearOrderClass.

tests.name: nat_le
tests.statement: The code of (ℕ, ≤) is in linearOrderClass; the code of (ℕ, <) is not.

tests.name: all_true
tests.statement: The code relating every pair fails antisymmetry.

tests.name: divisibility
tests.statement: The code of divisibility on ℕ is a partial order that is not total.

tests.name: well_orders
tests.statement: Adding the diagonal to a code of exists_mem_wellOrderClass_type_eq gives a code in linearOrderClass for each ω ≤ β < ω₁.

targets.name: blockOrder
targets.statement: For a graph code c, the linear order on List ℚ × ℕ: lexicographic, first by List ℚ, then inside the block of x by the order of type ω + (χ_c(x) + 2) putting indices ≥ χ_c(x)+2 first; relabelled to ℕ along a fixed bijection.

locator.where: Lemma VI.18, lines 4286–4288 (replace a labelled point by a finite order with label + 2 elements)

api.name: blockOrder_linear
api.statement: The order is a linear order for every code.

api.name: blockOrder_continuous
api.statement: Each comparison depends on two colours, so the map is continuous.

api.name: finite_condensation_classes
api.statement: The maximal sets in which any two points bound a finite interval and that are finite are exactly the final finite parts of the blocks, of size χ_c(x)+2.

tests.name: omega_part_infinite
tests.statement: A point of the ω-part and the first point of the finite part of the same block bound an infinite interval.

tests.name: root_block
tests.statement: The block of [] has finite part of size χ_c([]) + 2, the same for all graphs.

tests.name: empty_vs_complete
tests.statement: The images of the empty graph and the complete graph on ℕ are not isomorphic.

targets.name: exists_continuous_reduction_graphClass_linearOrderClass
targets.statement: There is a continuous f : StructureSpace Language.graph → StructureSpace Language.order with f '' graphClass ⊆ linearOrderClass and, for c d ∈ graphClass, c ≅ d ↔ f c ≅ f d.

targets.name: borelComplete_linearOrderClass
targets.statement: BorelComplete linearOrderClass.

targets.name: treeClass
targets.statement: treeClass : Set (StructureSpace Language.order): codes whose decoded relation is a partial order with a least element in which every {y | y ≤ x} is finite and linearly ordered.

locator.where: lines 257–263 (rooted binary trees as partial orders, the binary case; the definition of treeClass is the roadmap's own)

api.name: measurableSet_treeClass
api.statement: treeClass is Borel and invariant.

api.name: not_isClosed_treeClass
api.statement: treeClass is not closed.

api.name: treeClass_iso_prefix
api.statement: Members are isomorphic to infinite prefix-closed sets of lists (target 3.12).

tests.name: chain_and_star
tests.statement: The codes of (ℕ, ≤) and of the star (0 below all, others incomparable) are in treeClass.

tests.name: integers_reverse
tests.statement: (ℤ, ≤) transported (no least element) and (ℕ, ≥) (infinite down-sets) are not.

tests.name: not_closed
tests.statement: The chains n < n−1 < … < 0 < n+1 < … are in treeClass and converge to the code of (ℕ, ≥).

targets.name: tagTree
targets.statement: For a graph code c, the order on List ℚ × Option ℕ: (x, none) ordered by prefix; tag nodes (x, some m) above (x, none) and its ancestors; (x, some 0) below the other tags of x; (x, some m) ≤ (x, some m') for 0 < m ≤ m' ≤ χ_c(x)+1; tags with m > χ_c(x)+1 are leaves above (x, some 0); relabelled to ℕ.

locator.where: Lemma VI.18, lines 4205–4245 (labelled trees of tuples, infinitely repeated)

api.name: tagTree_mem_treeClass
api.statement: The relabelled code is in treeClass.

api.name: original_iff_infinite_chain
api.statement: A node is original iff an infinite chain starts at it.

api.name: tag_height
api.statement: The subtree above (x, some 0) has height χ_c(x)+2, the unique non-original child of (x, none).

tests.name: heights
tests.statement: χ = 0 gives height 2, χ = 1 height 3.

tests.name: surplus
tests.statement: Surplus leaves change no height.

tests.name: untagged
tests.statement: Without tags the original nodes form the same tree for every c.

targets.name: borelComplete_treeClass
targets.statement: BorelComplete treeClass, through a continuous reduction from graphClass.

targets.name: treeClass_iff_descriptiveTree
targets.statement: For c ∈ treeClass there is an infinite T ∈ Descriptive.tree ℕ with the decoded order of c isomorphic to (T, prefix order), and every infinite T ∈ Descriptive.tree ℕ with the prefix order is isomorphic to the decoded order of some c ∈ treeClass.

locator.where: lines 276–281 (rooted binary trees identified with subtrees of 2^{<ℕ}, the binary case)

tests.name: finite_tree
tests.statement: {[], [0], [1], [0,0]} is finite and has no code on ℕ.

tests.name: full_tree
tests.statement: The full tree List ℕ gives a code in treeClass.

targets.name: borelComplete_rootedGraphTree
targets.statement: In the relational language with one binary and one unary symbol, the class of codes of connected acyclic graphs with exactly one marked vertex is invariant Borel and Borel complete, by the Borel (not continuous) reduction from treeClass sending an order to its cover graph with the least element marked.

tests.name: ray
tests.statement: (ℕ, ≤) gives a ray with its end marked; marking vertex 1 instead gives a non-isomorphic code.

tests.name: star
tests.statement: The star gives a star with its centre marked.

layers.title: Borel S∞-spaces and the universal embedding

targets.name: instMeasurableSpacePerm
targets.statement: Equiv.Perm ℕ carries borel of the base topology, with BorelSpace and StandardBorelSpace; a Borel S∞-space is X with [MeasurableSpace X] [StandardBorelSpace X] [MulAction (Equiv.Perm ℕ) X] [MeasurableSMul₂ (Equiv.Perm ℕ) X], with orbit relation MulAction.orbitRel.

api.name: measurableSMul₂_structureSpace
api.statement: The logic action on StructureSpace L (countable relational) is a Borel S∞-space with orbit relation structureIsoSetoid L.

api.name: measurableSMul₂_subtype
api.statement: An invariant Borel subset of a Borel S∞-space is one.

api.name: image_equivariant_injective
api.statement: An equivariant measurable injection between Borel S∞-spaces has invariant Borel image (Lusin–Souslin) and reduces the orbit relations.

tests.name: evaluation_action

tests.name: trivial_action

tests.name: uncountable_language
tests.statement: For uncountably many unary symbols the coding space carries the product σ-algebra of uncountably many copies of Bool, in which no singleton is measurable (a measurable set depends on countably many coordinates), while a standard Borel space has measurable singletons; so it is not standard Borel. Cardinality does not decide this, since 2^ℵ₁ = 2^ℵ₀ is consistent with ZFC.

targets.name: universalLanguage
targets.statement: universalLanguage : FirstOrder.Language.{0,0}, relational, with exactly one relation symbol of each arity n.

api.name: structureSpace_universal_polish

tests.name: arity_count

tests.name: one_point_code

tests.name: not_ℕ_symbols
tests.statement: The language with countably many symbols of each arity is not universalLanguage; the coding of 4.4 maps it injectively into universalLanguage.

targets.name: anchoredCode
targets.statement: For a Polish S∞-space X (continuous action) with a countable basis (S_n): the code in the language with countably many symbols of each arity whose (k, n)-th symbol holds of a : Fin k → ℕ at x iff ∃ g, (∀ i, g (a i) = i) ∧ g • x ∈ S_n.

locator.where: proof sketch of Theorem 2.1 and Corollary 2.2, lines 247–268

api.name: anchoredCode_isOpen
api.statement: Each coordinate set {x | …} is open, a union of translates g⁻¹ • S_n; the map is measurable.

api.name: anchoredCode_smul
api.statement: The map is equivariant for the logic action (substitute g' = g h).

api.name: anchoredCode_injective
api.statement: The map is injective: anchors (0,…,k−1) give pointwise stabilizers converging to 1.

tests.name: evaluation_marks
tests.statement: X = ℕ, S_n = {n}: the (1,0)-th symbol holds of (a) at x iff x = a; for g = (0 1), Φ 1 holds at (1) and not at (0).

tests.name: one_point
tests.statement: One-point X with S_0 = X: the (k,0)-th symbol holds exactly of injective tuples.

tests.name: no_anchor
tests.statement: Without the anchoring g (a i) = i the map is constant on orbits, not injective for X = ℕ.

targets.name: unpairCode
targets.statement: The map from codes of the language with countably many symbols of each arity to StructureSpace universalLanguage reading symbol m on b : Fin m → ℕ as the (k, n)-th symbol on b ∘ Fin.castLE, (n, k) = Nat.unpair m; continuous, injective, equivariant.

api.name: unpairCode_injective
api.statement: The (k,n)-th symbol at a is recovered at m = Nat.pair n k on any extension of a.

api.name: unpairCode_smul
api.statement: The map commutes with the logic action.

tests.name: pair_zero
tests.statement: Nat.unpair 0 = (0,0): the arity-0 symbol of universalLanguage reads the (0,0)-th symbol.

tests.name: padding_irrelevant
tests.statement: The value at m does not depend on the entries of b beyond k.

tests.name: not_surjective
tests.statement: The map is not surjective: its image consists of codes whose arity-m relation depends only on the first k entries.
